tools.notes: Qualified on version family per environment-spec.md (changed 2026-07-29 from exact servicing revision, so Patch Tuesday no longer silently downgrades runs); the exact revision is recorded per manifest.

Pinned in environment-spec.md. Server-side only: it is present on the estate member server and absent on the client guest, so a lane may use it to author or inspect a topology but may not rely on it as a client-side oracle.

Recorded, not qualified (changed 2026-07-29): no current lane executes LGPO, so its hash is provenance only. Ruled 2026-08-03 that placing LGPO.exe on the estate is acceptable — disposable, checkpoint-backed guests, and the isolation invariant governs egress rather than what is deliberately placed inside — so WP-5 keeps its LGPO leg and this row is not pending because the tool was ruled out. It is pending because qualification is earned by execution: WP-5 must push the binary post-restore, verify it on the guest against a pinned SHA-256, and only then restore the check in frozen_environment_violations(). Do not flip this row on the strength of the ruling alone.

tools.notes: Requalified by the WI-059 computer and user RSoP scenarios on the 26200 client. The client has no GroupPolicy module. Computer capture explicitly selects /scope:computer; user capture selects /scope:user /user <principal> and requires a verified interactive session. Qualification requires the output artifact, not merely exit zero.

Not used by any lane, and the reason is worth keeping. This row stood in for the user-scope gap: WP-6 forbids an interactive `whoami /groups` as the computer token, and the collection it described rode an interactive logon the estate did not have. The estate has one now (windows-evidence-lab, the `user-logged-on` checkpoint), and WP-9 was built without whoami: the principal's SID comes from an NTAccount translation, the winning values from the loaded hive at HKEY_USERS\<SID>, and the resultant set from gpresult /scope:user /user <principal>. Kept as a row rather than deleted so the gate it represented is visibly closed rather than quietly removed.

Finalization refuses working/index/HEAD byte drift before writing a verdict or tag, including with --no-tag. WP-0 binds its finalizer and shared library in its manifest.

lanes.oracle: LGPO import, policy refresh, direct registry API reads, and GroupPolicy operational events on a snapshot-backed endpoint, plus domain-GPO processing through the verified WP-2 path.
lanes.notes: Hosts qualified 2026-08-03; now blocked only on lgpo, which the 2026-08-03 ruling keeps in the lane rather than narrowing it away. The binary must be pushed post-restore over psdirect and hash-verified on the guest, so no golden checkpoint carries it. The domain-GPO leg is the one that tests Studio (its output reaching a client through SYSVOL); the LGPO leg mostly tests Microsoft's tool, and WP-5 acceptance requires both.

lanes.oracle: gpresult.exe /x <file> /f /scope:computer on the client, parsed from the http://www.microsoft.com/GroupPolicy/Rsop namespace, plus direct winning-registry reads, GroupPolicy operational events, LDAP tokenGroups via [adsisearcher] for the computer token, and Get-Acl / Get-GPPermission -All for effective rights.
lanes.notes: Requalified 2026-10-09 at de9736ed3a4148b91cf2267fbe4640e260cc232f by rsop-observe-20261009002514-3293, rsop-observe-20261009002658-3387, rsop-observe-20261009002841-9327, rsop-observe-20261009003024-5445, rsop-observe-20261009003207-9958, rsop-observe-20261009005022-4207, rsop-observe-20261009003349-5735. The seven computer scenarios cover precedence, block/enforcement/disabled links, true/false/error WMI outcomes, allow/read-only/deny filtering, group deny, and deny Read. The group-denial case reboots and verifies a refreshed machine token. Applied-GPO comparison and direct winning-registry reads are gated; neither can substitute for the other. The client uses gpresult because its GroupPolicy module is absent. SearchedSOM freshness is not graded; WI-028 requires separate scoping evidence.

lanes.oracle: gpresult.exe /x <file> /f /scope:user /user <DOMAIN>\<principal> on the client, parsed from the http://www.microsoft.com/GroupPolicy/Rsop namespace's UserResults section, plus the winning HKCU values read from the principal's loaded hive at HKEY_USERS\<SID>, plus GroupPolicy operational events -- 8005 for the completion of the principal's own processing pass, and 5311 for the loopback mode Windows actually used.
lanes.notes: Requalified 2026-10-09 at de9736ed3a4148b91cf2267fbe4640e260cc232f by rsop-user-observe-20261009003535-1462, rsop-user-observe-20261009003744-5527, rsop-user-observe-20261009003952-3546, rsop-user-observe-20261009004238-6019, rsop-user-observe-20261009004533-3353, rsop-user-observe-20261009004749-4067. Six scenarios cover loopback merge/replace, disabled user side, allow/read-only/group filtering, explicit deny Apply and deny Read. Applied-GPO comparison is gated (WI-032); winning values are read from the principal's loaded HKEY_USERS hive. Event 5311 verifies loopback mode and a mode mismatch is inconclusive. Group cases restart the client and verify the new session token contains the authored group. A verified console session is required. User-side WMI outcomes and slow-link processing remain outside scope; SearchedSOM freshness is not graded.

lanes.oracle: Native Backup-GPO, Restore-GPO, Import-GPO (into an existing GPO and with -CreateIfNeeded) and Copy-GPO (with and without -CopyAcl) on the member server, every call pinned to the PDC emulator. After each operation the target is read back (Get-GPO, Get-GPRegistryValue, Get-GPPermission -All, gPCWQLFilter, and Get-GPInheritance on the run's OUs), and each of six dimensions (settings, GUID, DACL, WMI association, links, description) is classified kept/replaced/lost/defaulted against the source, the target's prior state and an untouched New-GPO control. The expectation (lifecycle.SCOPE_SURVIVAL plus each restore plan's claims) is built on the controller and never sent to the guest.

lanes.notes: Qualified 2026-10-09 at de9736ed3a4148b91cf2267fbe4640e260cc232f by report-parity-20261009001727-3532 (26/26 checks, 30/30 cases plus the authored case; release 1.1.0 batch, 2026-10-09). Item identity (element, name, uid, action) and order only; preference Properties beyond action, ADMX <Policy> rendering, Scripts, links, security filtering and WMI filters are named exclusions. No Studio defect is accepted: the WI-072 and WI-073 cases must agree exactly.

lanes.oracle: Two legs on disposable unlinked GPOs. Read: New-NetFirewallRule/Set-NetFirewallProfile -PolicyStore author the policy and Studio's codec parses Windows' Registry.pol. Write: Import-GPO of Studio's backup, then Windows' Registry.pol is compared byte for byte with the candidate's. Both legs read the policy back through the NetSecurity cmdlets and Get-GPOReport. Endpoint application is outside this lane.
lanes.notes: Certified 2026-10-09 at de9736ed3a4148b91cf2267fbe4640e260cc232f by firewall-20261009001906-2614294 (36/36). The 13 measured rule shapes and the Domain/Private profile tranche parse with zero unrecognised records, Windows returns Studio's Registry.pol unchanged after Import-GPO, and cmdlet readback matches on both legs including six named normalizations. Studio's export registers the firewall tool GUID (B05566AC) for firewall-only machine policy, as native authoring does, and the write leg carried exactly the native pair; GPMC's report rendered the firewall extension for both legs, and GPME editability was not measured (WI-077). One build (WS2025 26100) was measured. IPsec, Public Key, wired and wireless policy are out of scope.

lanes.oracle: For each case, a GPMC-format backup carrying fdeploy1.ini and the fdeploy.ini marker is imported with Import-GPO into a disposable unlinked GPO. SYSVOL is read back, a fresh Get-GPOReport -ReportType Xml is taken and Backup-GPO re-exports the GPO. The re-exported files must be byte-identical to the candidate's, and Studio's read_backup over Windows' own backup must agree with the report's FolderRedirectionSettings rows (folder id, principal SID, destination path). The expectation is built on the controller and never reaches the guest.
lanes.notes: Certified 2026-10-09 at de9736ed3a4148b91cf2267fbe4640e260cc232f by fd-20261009002120-4293 (29/29). Four cases: R3's GPMC-written bytes verbatim (Flags 1021) and three builder-written Flags-only variants (1020, 1023, 3069); one folder (Documents), one principal (Everyone), one path. Certifies the reader's agreement with Windows for these shapes only. Flags is carried, not decoded: Windows' option rendering per value is recorded, not asserted (WI-066 data). Multi-folder and multi-principal documents, other Flags values, the writer (WI-066/R12) and endpoint application are not covered. One build (WS2025 26100) was measured.
